name: XLR 3-pin (balanced audio)
description: The locking 3-pin circular connector used for balanced analog audio (microphones, line level, PA). Balanced means the signal travels as a hot/cold differential pair with a shield; the receiver subtracts cold from hot, cancelling any noise picked up equally on both. The modern standard is 'pin 2 hot' (AES14).

contacts.name: HOT
contacts.description: signal +, in phase (hot). 'Pin 2 hot' is the AES/modern standard

variants: Pin 2 hot (AES14) is universal now; a handful of vintage gear wired pin 3 hot, which just inverts polarity (audible only when mixed with a pin-2-hot source).
XLR also appears in 4/5/6+ pin variants (intercom, DMX-on-3-or-5-pin, headset) -- physically similar shell, different pinout; don't assume 3-pin audio.
DMX512 lighting uses a 5-pin (or, non-compliantly, 3-pin) XLR -- electrically RS-485, NOT audio. Never plug audio gear into a DMX line.
gotchas: Balanced (XLR) vs unbalanced (TS): an XLR carries hot/cold/ground and rejects noise over long runs; that's why mics use it. Adapting XLR to unbalanced TS ties cold to ground and loses the noise rejection.
Pin 1 (shield) should tie to chassis ground at the input end; lifting or mis-wiring pin 1 is a classic hum/ground-loop source.
Male XLR = output/source, female = input/sink (signal flows into the female). Cables are male-on-one-end, female-on-the-other, following the signal.
notes: 3-pin XLR balanced-audio pinout (1=GND, 2=hot, 3=cold) per AES14 'pin 2 hot'. DMX/multi-pin variants noted as distinct.
